title: Chocolate collar
subtitle: a curved strip of tempered chocolate wrapped around a cake or dessert
excerpt: A chocolate collar wraps around the outside of a round cake or mousse, holding the filling and creating a smooth, glossy exterior. The collar is made by spreading tempered chocolate onto an acetate strip, letting it set to a leather-like state, then wrapping it around the cake and peeling the acetate away once fully set.
sourceNotes: Chocolate collar technique used in professional pâtisserie; technique widely taught in UK and French confectionery training from the mid-twentieth century onward.

glossaryTerms.definition: The process of melting and cooling chocolate through specific temperatures to stabilise its cocoa-butter crystals, giving it a high gloss, a snap when broken, and a smooth melt in the mouth.
A clear flexible plastic sheet used in pâtisserie as a mould lining and to create chocolate collars. Chocolate releases cleanly from acetate once set.

Cut the acetate to the exact height and circumference of your cake. For a 20 cm round, cut a strip about 65 cm long (the circumference plus 2 cm for overlap) and as tall as the cake. Wipe it with a clean cloth to remove any dust or fingerprints; marks will show through the chocolate.
Melt 200 g of dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water, stirring regularly, until it reaches 50 to 55°C. Keep the base of the bowl clear of the water.

Remove from the heat. Pour two-thirds of the chocolate onto a clean marble or granite surface and work it with a palette knife and scraper, spreading and gathering, until it cools to 27°C. It will thicken noticeably.
Return the cooled chocolate to the bowl with the remaining third. Stir until the combined temperature reads 31 to 32°C. The chocolate is now tempered: it will be fluid, glossy, and set with a snap.
Pour the tempered chocolate onto the acetate strip and spread it evenly with a palette knife to the edges. Aim for about 2 to 3 mm thick.
Wait 2 to 3 minutes until the chocolate is set enough to hold its shape but still flexible when bent (the leather stage). If it cracks when you flex it, it has gone too far.
Pick up the acetate strip and wrap it around the cake, chocolate-side in. Secure the join with a small strip of tape on the acetate. Refrigerate for 20 minutes until fully set.
Peel the acetate away carefully, starting from one end. The collar will stay in place on the cake, revealing a high-gloss surface.

attrs.problem: Chocolate cracking when wrapped around the cake
attrs.avoid: Avoid waiting too long at room temperature; once chocolate is past the leather stage it will snap.
attrs.fix: Work in a cooler room or have the collar spread and ready to wrap as soon as it is barely set.

attrs.problem: Dull or streaky finish after peeling
attrs.avoid: Avoid inadequate tempering; un-tempered chocolate blooms grey and streaky as it cools.
attrs.fix: Re-temper the chocolate and make a fresh strip; there is no way to recover a bloomed collar once set.
